text:
The great hero also completes the six perfections.
He is close to omniscience.
“Furthermore, Subhūti, when bodhisattva great beings practicing the six perfections see beings born in the four abodes—those born from an egg,
those born from a womb,
those born from moisture,
and those born spontaneously—they should think like this:
‘In whatever way I may fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening, in that buddhafield of mine there will be no beings born from an egg,
no beings born from a womb,
The three places that arise from moisture would not occur and would not be possible.
Otherwise, all sentient beings would be born miraculously.
In that way, one should practice the six perfections.
One should purify a buddhafield.
One should bring sentient beings to maturity.’
Sūbhadra, a bodhisattva-mahasattva who practices in that way
completes the six perfections
and approaches omniscience.
“Furthermore, Sūbhadra, a bodhisattva-mahasattva who practices the perfection of wisdom should not stand in the notion that ‘form is empty.’
When the great hero practices the six perfections,
if he sees beings who lack the five superknowledges,
he should examine himself thus:
“In whatever way I may
